task.description: Implement REQ-228 (entity event registration + create/update/delete record commands) exactly per the CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR-approved design doc: Letflow.EventStore.append_multi/3 (composable extraction of append/2's M1-M6 Multi steps), Letflow.Entities.EventTypes.seed!/1 (registers ENTITY_RECORD_CREATED/UPDATED/DELETED via the existing Registry.register_type/2), Letflow.Entities.Records (create_record/2, update_record/2, delete_record/2), Letflow.Entities.Record.Latest and Letflow.Entities.EntityTypeInstance schemas plus their tenant-scoped migrations, and a full ExUnit test suite covering all 8 acceptance criteria.

result.note: mix compile --warnings-as-errors: clean, zero warnings. mix format --check-formatted: clean, zero diffs. mix test test/letflow/entities/records_test.exs: 21/21 passed (covers AC1-AC8: event-type registration x2, create atomicity + forced-failure rollback proof, idempotent-replay parity x2, REQ-227 validation rejection x2, per-entity-TYPE synthetic-instance mapping x2, outer-envelope vs inner-validation independent exercise x2, update/delete command behavior x6, definition-resolution edge cases x2, no-route-file scope check x2). Regression: mix test test/letflow/event_store/ -> 150/150 passed (confirms append_multi/3's extraction did not alter append/2's or append_platform_event/2's own behavior). mix test test/letflow/entities/ -> 84/84 passed (REQ-225/226/227 unaffected). mix test test/letflow/engine/ -> 977 passed (1 property, 976 tests), 16 excluded, 0 failures (confirms TaskActivation.append_multi/6's own usage and every other append/2 caller in the engine are unaffected). git diff --stat confirms zero route/controller files touched (AC8's scope check). Two infra fixes made along the way, both required for the shared test-tenant-clone template to reflect the new migrations, not part of REQ-228's own application code: (1) dropped the stale 'tenant_template' Postgres schema so it rebuilds against the new migration manifest; (2) updated the two pre-existing hardcoded '39 expected tenant tables' assertions (test/support/tenant_fixture.ex's own list plus test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_test.exs's oracle test) to 41, adding entity_record_latest/entity_type_instances -- same bump pattern every prior table-adding requirement (REQ-226 et al.) already made in that file's own comment trail.
discrepancies_flagged_for_security_revie: entity_type_instance_guard (design §3.2) is implemented as a plain, eager Letflow.Entities.EntityTypeInstance.get_or_create/2 call BEFORE any Ecto.Multi is built, not as a lazy Multi.run/3 step inside the same Multi as append_multi/3's own steps. Root cause: Letflow.EventStore.append_multi/3's attrs[:instance_id] must be a concrete UUID value at Multi-COMPOSITION time (plain Elixir code, before Repo.transaction/1 ever runs), but a lazy Multi.run/3 step's result is only available inside `changes` at transaction EXECUTION time -- a structural incompatibility between the design's literal §3.2 'Multi.run(:entity_type_instance_guard, ...)' framing and §3.1's append_multi/3 signature. get_or_create/2's own race-safe insert-if-absent-then-re-select protocol (identical idiom to assign_sequence/3/claim_idempotency/3) preserves the same correctness guarantee; AC2's atomicity claim (event append + entity_record_latest write, one transaction) is unaffected since entity_type_instances is not part of that transaction boundary. Full reasoning documented in Letflow.Entities.EntityTypeInstance's own moduledoc.

entity_def_version's outer-envelope JSON type: the design's own §4.1 table declares 'entity_def_version':{'type':'integer'} while simultaneously stating (same section) it carries entity_definitions.logical_shape_version's role -- a :binary content-hash column, never an integer. Registered here as {'type':'string'} instead, with logical_shape_version hex-encoded (Base.encode16/2, lowercase) for the JSON envelope and stored/round-tripped as raw :binary in entity_record_latest.entity_def_version and in Records' in-memory command context. This resolves the design's own explicitly-named open question §8 item 1 ('left for ELIXIR-DEV/REQ-229 to confirm ... not silently picked here'). Documented in Letflow.Entities.EventTypes's moduledoc.

Real gap the design doc does not mention at all: Letflow.Entities.Definitions.get_definition_by_name/2 always returns a freshly-queried EntityDefinition whose definition_json decodes from jsonb as a STRING-keyed map with string-valued 'type' entries (confirmed against DefinitionsTest's own reloaded.definition_json["name"] assertion), but Letflow.Entities.Record.Validator.build_record_schema/1 (REQ-227) expects REQ-225's Definition.t() shape verbatim -- ATOM-keyed, with type: holding an atom. Passing the persisted definition_json straight into validate_record_payload/2 would silently produce zero violations (Map.get(json, :fields, []) finds no :fields atom key), the worst possible validation-gate failure mode. Letflow.Entities.Records's own private definition_document/1 converts the persisted map back into the atom-keyed shape (String.to_existing_atom/1 on 'type', safe because the closed field-type atom set is already compiled in via Definition.Validator/Record.Validator) before ever calling validate_record_payload/2. Documented in Letflow.Entities.Records's own moduledoc.

Design §6.2's literal 'unique_index(:entity_type_instances, [:entity_type])' (redundant with the table's own primary key on that same single column) was confirmed, empirically, to collide with test/support/tenant_template.ex's LIKE-based clone-and-rename tooling (Postgrex 42P07 duplicate_table on the index name during every subsequent test-tenant clone). Removed from the migration; Letflow.Entities.EntityTypeInstance.insert_changeset/2's unique_constraint/3 now targets the primary key's own default index name (:entity_type_instances_pkey) instead. AC5's 'exactly one row per entity TYPE' guarantee is unaffected -- the primary key alone already enforces it at the database level. Documented in the migration file's own comment.
